title: A Pulsed Field Gradient NMR Study of Self-Diffusion in a Polydisperse Polymer System: Dextran in Water
abstract: Self-diffusion coefficients have been obtained over a range o f concentrations for dextran in deuterated water. The dextran samples were all derived from Leuconostoc mesenteroides strain B512 and were polydisperse, with M, values o f 10 500,40 100, 75 800, 170 000, and 461 000 daltons. The implications of polydispersity for the pulsed field gradient experiment are considered. We observation of a molar mass weighted self-diffusion coefficient, (D),, under conditions o f ensemble averaging and verify this using a mixture of well-characterized monodisperse polystyrene with differing molar masses in CCl, solution. The dextran data obey DL1 = D0-'(l + k ~ ) except for the lowest molar mass, where anomalous behavior is observed. We find Do -M4.57(2) and note consistency with Do values obtained by fluorescent labeling methods for two other molar masses. The kf values for dextran/D20 are molar mass independent, in contradiction with theory. In the semidilute regime of 170000-dalton dextran/DpO, a concentration-dependent scaling behavior is found with D, N in accordance with the de Gennes reptation theory modified to allow for crossover effects. An upper limit to the dextran side-chain lengths of 10 monomer units is implied.
